column4: class BaseOperationType(Enum) declares INDEX, CREATE, DELETE, UPDATE, APPEND. Docstrings verbatim: 'DELETE (str): deletes an existing record.' 'UPDATE (str): updates or overwrites an existing record.' 'INDEX (str): creates a new record with a specific ID.'

column1: storage backend
column4: 🔴 default_operation_type = BaseOperationType.INDEX. INDEX writes to a SPECIFIC ID, so a re-write carrying an existing statement id OVERWRITES it

column4: 🔴 ZERO occurrences of append-only, WORM, or any immutability/retention MODE. There is no course-scoped deletion either: deletion is per-record, by id, at the backend

column1: # THE VERDICT: ralph is append-only AT THE API LAYER AND NOWHERE ELSE. The audit record's
# protection is THE ABSENCE OF AN HTTP ROUTE, not a guarantee of the store. A holder of
# Elasticsearch or MongoDB credentials deletes or overwrites statements with ralph's OWN
# CLI, in one documented option.
# 🔴 LIMB 2 FIRES. Pattern 32 step 3 needs a WORM store beside the LRS and the estimate grows.
# WHY THIS IS A TREND AND NOT A ONE-OFF: it is the SECOND INDEPENDENT INSTANCE of p187's
# dotty-tutor finding. There, the teacher's `corrected_assessment` — the human's override of
# an AI grade — was ondelete=CASCADE from two parents. Here, the LRS that would hold the same
# record has no immutability at all. Two unrelated projects, same defect class: 🔴 the
# human-oversight record is protected by CONVENTION, never by the STORE. Three regimes now
# require that record (NA: Oklahoma, Maryland; EU: Annex III high-risk assessment; APAC:
# Vietnam Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg names automated grading of students a high-risk system).
